newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rican inflation rises 13.8 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rican inflation rises 13.8 pct in 1996.

text.p: Consumer prices rose 13.8 percent in Costa Rica in 1996, down from 22.5 percent in 1995, the government said Tuesday.

Economy Minister Jose Leon Desanti told a news conference that foreign factors most influenced Costa Rican inflation, notably higher world oil prices as well as the seasonal importing of some agricultural products to Costa Rica.
Inflation in the month of December was 1.08 percent, down from 1.15 percent in December 1995, he said.
"The cost of living for Costa Ricans was affected by an increase in the international price of hydrocarbons," Desanti said.
The importing of some agricultural products when they were out of season in Costa Rica also affected consumers, he said.
He mentioned wheat, rice and beans, which are staples of the Costa Rican diet.
